title: Ancient proteins identify various Denisovan remains from Southwest China.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the PRIDE (proteomics data archive) project PXD073112 by keyword search and pulled its file listing through the API: 100 files totalling 31.9 GB. There are 33 RAW mass-spectrometry files of 0.5–1.4 GB each, 31 peak-list files (MGF format, up to 274 MB), 29 zipped identification files (mzIdentML, under 9 MB each), 6 FASTA sequence files and a README.xlsx. Names show hominin samples (26S0135, 26S0136, …) and blank negative-control runs (BK). I opened none of the files.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The counts come from the abstract and PRIDE description, not the files: 60,000 fragments screened, 76 sent to ZooMS (collagen peptide fingerprinting), 17 sent to shotgun proteomics, and 5 hominin specimens assigned to Denisovans via the variant COL1A2 R996K. Not open access, so no full text and no supplement was read. The ZooMS spectra for the 76 fragments do not appear in this PRIDE listing.

a1_downloadable.note: PRIDE PXD073112 is public and its file listing came back without a login (checked via the API). The files themselves were not downloaded.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table pairs a specimen with its taxon. The Denisovan label is the paper's conclusion, inferred from variant peptides and phylogenetics, and would have to be built from the identification files plus the paper's text.

a3_inputs_present.note: Spectra and peptide identifications are present as files (seen in the listing), but they are raw or semi-processed mass-spectrometry data, not a feature table.

a4_units_stated.note: Mass-spectrometry formats carry m/z (mass-to-charge ratio) and intensity by standard. Not opened.

a5_enough_rows.note: Only 5 labelled hominin specimens (from the paper), plus a few blanks; at most 17 proteomic samples and 76 ZooMS fragments. That is far below the ~400 rows needed even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 31.9 GB total, ~30 GB of it RAW
a6_fits_laptop.note: The usable mzIdentML/MGF subset (~1–2 GB) would fit, but RAW files are off-limits and the n is the binding problem anyway.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Sample codes in the listing are consistent with a handful of specimens plus blanks; exact per-specimen counts were not cross-checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: The taxon label is inferred from the same peptide spectra a model would use as input (diagnostic SAPs, i.e. single amino-acid polymorphisms), so the label is computed from the features.

existing_models.name: SpecieScan (Bioinformatics 2024), automated taxon identification from ZooMS MALDI-TOF (a mass-spectrometry method) spectra
existing_models.score_and_split: >90% genus-level accuracy on spectra from Palaeolithic sites (from the search snippet; split not checked)

existing_models.name: isoBLAST / ClassiCOL (J Proteome Res 2025), taxonomic classification of collagen from LC-MS/MS (liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry)

integration.partner_dataset: Other PRIDE palaeoproteomics hominin projects (e.g. PXD063518, PXD054412, PXD047932, PXD058447)
integration.join_key: none standard; per-specimen taxon assignments from each paper
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Pooling every hominin palaeoproteome still gives only tens of specimens, too few to model.

controls.negative_control: Blank extraction runs (BK files) exist in PRIDE.

honest_claim_h3: With 5 labelled specimens, no model can claim anything; the paper's taxon calls come from rule-based variant-peptide matching, not learning.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use ancient bone protein mass spectra to predict which species or hominin group a bone fragment came from.
plain_idea.train_on: Mass-spectrometry peptide spectra from bone and tooth fragments; 5 hominin specimens plus blanks have a published label (from the paper), and the 76 ZooMS fragments are not in this deposit.
plain_idea.predict: The taxon (Denisovan, other hominin, or other mammal). The true answer comes from expert matching of diagnostic peptide variants, which uses the same spectra.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Faster triage of tens of thousands of bone fragments would help palaeoproteomics labs, but that needs large ZooMS reference sets, not this 5-specimen deposit.

label_elsewhere.sources: Other PRIDE hominin palaeoproteomics projects found by searching PRIDE (about 10 Denisovan or Homo-related projects); ZooMS reference spectra sets used by SpecieScan (known from the search).
label_elsewhere.join_key: none standard (per-specimen IDs inside each paper)
label_elsewhere.why: Even pooled, hominin specimens with protein-based labels number in the tens, not the hundreds.

ml_idea: Taxon classification from palaeoproteomic spectra. It is infeasible here because there are 5 labelled specimens and the label is derived from the same spectra.

effort.compute_note: Sizes come from the PRIDE file listing; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled specimens: 5 (from the paper), which kills the project.

verdict_reason: Five labelled Denisovan specimens in a 31.9 GB mostly raw proteomics deposit (PRIDE PXD073112). The taxon label is inferred from the same peptide spectra a model would see as input. The project fails A2, A5, A6 and A8.
